title: Document include authoring and dependency-driven regeneration
description:
Design-only planning requested by Ryan during voice. Implementation remains unstarted; no code, infrastructure, deployment, purchase or publishing authorization is implied. Initial status stays open (Discovery), unassigned.

As a page author and publication operator, I want a current include authoring and regeneration guide, so that I can compose pages and diagnose public updates without maintaining parallel dependency rules.

Acceptance behavior (planned, not executable or verified yet):
```gherkin
Feature: Document include authoring and dependency-driven regeneration
  Scenario: Follow the authoring and operations guide
    Given the supported include behavior and its implementation status are documented
    When an author composes a single-page include or selected list and an operator follows a saved public change
    Then the guide explains parsing, site-wide dependency-index updates and actual affected-page regeneration
    And it explains nested and transitive includes, cycle reports and deduplicated regeneration
    And it covers stale-entry replacement or removal, old/new type or featured matches and unpublish
    And it explains publication isolation, public draft exclusion, retryable failures and stale-version protection
    And RSS and Atom eligibility is documented separately from ordinary page or wiki membership
    And examples distinguish proposed include syntax from verified shipped capability
```

Final agreed authoring direction, planning only: “include” is the working construct name, not approved concrete syntax. It supports inclusion of a single page or a selected list. “Collection” means a selection of content, not a new storage object. On page/content save or compile, the supported pipeline scans/parses include constructs, updates the generated site-wide dependency index, and actually uses that index to regenerate affected pages; merely recording dependencies is incomplete. Reuse each include's rendering selection as the sole source of invalidation selection, with separate enforced publication/access/published gates. Nested/transitive includes, cycles, deduplication, edits/deletion and retries require observable behavior, not arbitrary-code inference.

RSS/Atom feed eligibility is distinct from page existence, include membership and navigation. An ordinary static wiki/help or product page does not automatically become a feed entry. Define shared feed selection/metadata and editorial eligibility without building a separate page or wiki engine. Exact include syntax, extension ownership and selection schema remain design questions; current Anth.us custom Python homepage code is evidence of a migration gap, not proof the proposed include construct is shipped.

Coordinate documentation epic PPY-9ad680 and its cross-cutting delivery and Help review tasks. Once syntax and ownership are agreed and implemented, verify examples against the real parser and operator workflow; do not publish invented include markup now. Behavior acceptance belongs to PPY-b6ede164-fad8-45da-a242-51362c5f8285 and post-save PPY-defff04e-17b5-4e28-9bb5-df412601a102.
